Top band (7-8): Complex explanation of importance. Answer demonstrates a range of accurate and detailed knowledge and understanding that is relevant to the question. Students explain the relationship between different aspects of importance, for example over time or by linking causes and consequences.
Example: The Essex–Cecil rivalry was important because it revealed the dangerous factional politics of Elizabeth’s final years. After the deaths of Elizabeth’s four closest advisors between 1588 and 1591 — including William Cecil, Dudley, Walsingham, and Hatton — a power vacuum opened. Essex expected to become the Queen’s main advisor, but Elizabeth appointed Robert Cecil as Secretary of State instead. This infuriated Essex, who felt the position was his by right. The rivalry drove Essex to increasingly reckless behaviour — the Irish disaster of 1599, where he made an unauthorised truce with Tyrone and returned to England without orders, was partly motivated by fear that Cecil was undermining him. Ultimately, the rivalry pushed Essex towards his doomed rebellion in 1601. Cecil’s victory was significant because he then used his unchallenged position to secretly arrange the smooth succession of James VI of Scotland.
